rationale: Both texts narrate the same preaching-and-baptizing ministry, checkable directly by reading the two side by side: the Isaiah 40:3 quotation, the "brood of vipers" rebuke, and the axe-and-fruit warning match word for word in this app's own BSB text at several points, alongside small, equally checkable differences ("do not presume" against "do not begin," 40.3.9/42.3.8; "sandals I am not worthy to carry" against "the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie," 40.3.11/42.3.16). Luke's account also continues the Isaiah quotation two verses further and contains an entire block Matthew's range does not -- the crowd's specific ethical questions and John's answers, and the people wondering whether John is the Christ (42.3.10-15). The label is strong rather than explicit because neither Gospel names or cites the other as its source.
